symptom: An MUSD NTT integration built from the current bridge documentation targets transceiver addresses that are no longer enabled by the deployed managers.
prerequisites: The integration copied an NTT transceiver from prose/address documentation rather than resolving the active manager's transceiver set and peers.
The operation concerns the current mainnet MUSD NTT deployment.
diagnosticSteps: Assert each source/destination chain and select fixed blocks.
Read getTransceivers() on each active NTT manager and nttManager()/getWormholePeer() on each returned transceiver.
Compare those deployed references with the pinned official ntt-bridge-musd-mainnet deployment artifact and only then with descriptive documentation.
expected: The current documentation identifies the same enabled transceivers and peers as the live managers.
observed: The March 2026 official deployment repository and August 2026 fixed-block reads agree on replacement MUSD transceivers, while current bridge documentation still prints earlier values.
control: Four digest-joined historical transfers using the current graph completed across Mezo↔Ethereum and Mezo↔Base.
verifiedCause: The descriptive bridge address reference lags the official deployment artifact and deployed manager/transceiver graph.
safeMitigation: Do not copy bridge addresses into a writer. Resolve promoted registry identities once available, re-read manager/transceiver peers and pause state, construct version-correct instructions, simulate, and require destination redemption evidence. A successful source receipt is not completion.
limitations: This record does not make the evidence-backed routes an MDK support promise.
Peer, pause, capacity, fee, relayer, and implementation state remain volatile.
